title: Affine charts and base-change recovery for infinitesimal scheme pushouts
statement:
Let $T\to T^+$ be a thickening of schemes, meaning a closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-scheme], and let $T\to S$ be affine (inverse images of affine opens are affine). For an $S$-scheme $X$, a $T^+$-scheme $Y$, and an isomorphism over $T$, $U=X\times_S T\simeq Y\times_{T^+}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], form the pushouts $P=S\amalg_TT^+$ and $Z=X\amalg_UY$ [lem-sfb-scheme-affine-thickening-pushout]. The canonical maps
$$X\longrightarrow Z\times_P S,\qquad Y\longrightarrow Z\times_P T^+$$
are isomorphisms. For every affine open $P_0\subseteq P$, the inverse images $S_0\subseteq S$, $T^+_0\subseteq T^+$, and $T_0\subseteq T$ are affine. Write these four affine schemes as
$$P_0=\operatorname{Spec}R,\quad S_0=\operatorname{Spec}B,\quad T^+_0=\operatorname{Spec}A',\quad T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A.$$
Then $A'\to A$ is surjective with nil kernel and the canonical map $R\to B\times_A A'$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every affine open $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}E\subseteq Z$ mapping into $P_0$, its inverse images $X_0,Y_0,U_0$ in $X,Y,U$ are affine. Writing them as $\operatorname{Spec}D,\operatorname{Spec}C',\operatorname{Spec}C$, respectively, and putting $I=\ker(A'\to A)$, the canonical maps identify
$$C=D\otimes_B A=C'/IC',\qquad E=D\times_C C',\qquad E\otimes_R B=D,\qquad E\otimes_R A'=C'.$$
All identifications are of algebras over the indicated base rings and commute with restriction to smaller opens. In addition, if $H$ is any scheme and compatible maps $X\to H$, $Y\to H$ induce $h:Z\to H$, then for every open $H_0\subseteq H$, the inverse images of $X,Y,U$ over $H_0$ have pushout $h^{-1}(H_0)$. No flatness, finite-presentation or finite-order assumption is required.

proof.text:
First record explicitly the sheaf construction of a pushout $W=V\amalg_KK'$ with $K\to K'$ a thickening and $a:K\to V$ affine. Use $|K|=|K'|$ to regard $a$ as $a':|K'|\to|V|$. On $|V|$ set
$$\mathcal F(O)=\mathcal O_V(O)\times_{\mathcal O_K(a^{-1}O)}\mathcal O_{K'}((a')^{-1}O).$$
Operations and restrictions are coordinatewise. Matching pairs glue uniquely because sections of each structure sheaf glue uniquely; hence this is a sheaf of rings. Its restriction to an open $O$ is exactly the same construction on the three inverse-image open subschemes. This is an explicit construction, not an extra assertion taken from the proof of the existing pushout node.

source.place: Tag 07RT, lemma-pushout-along-thickening, first paragraph of proof

proof.text:
For affine $O=\operatorname{Spec}D\subseteq V$, the inverse image $K_O$ is affine by the hypothesis on $a$, and $K'_O$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-affine-scheme]. Write their rings $C,C'$. The closed immersion gives a surjection $C'\twoheadrightarrow C$. Let $E=D\times_C C'$. By [lem-sfb-ring-fibre-product-spectrum], its spectrum is the topological pushout of these spectra. Since $|K_O|\to|K'_O|$ is a homeomorphism, the induced $|O|\to|\operatorname{Spec}E|$ is a homeomorphism: its inverse is induced by the identity on $|O|$ and $a'$ on $|K'_O|$; the quotient description checks both composites. For $e=(d,c')\in E$, with common image $c\in C$, the inverse images of $D_E(e)$ are $D_D(d)$, $D_{C'}(c')$, and $D_C(c)$. The localization formula of that same node and the principal-open spectrum identification give
$$\mathcal F(D_D(d))=D_d\times_{C_c}C'_{c'}\cong E_e.$$
These comparisons are induced by projections and commute with further principal localization.

The basic opens in step 2 form a basis. Their sheaf comparisons agree on intersections because $D(e)\cap D(f)=D(ef)$ and the maps are the further localization maps. Thus for any open, restrict a section to these basic opens, apply the comparisons and glue; do the same with the inverse comparisons. This extends them to mutually inverse sheaf maps. Consequently $(|V|,\mathcal F)$ is a scheme, and its open over every affine $O\subseteq V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D\times_C C')$. The projections of $\mathcal F$ give scheme morphisms from $V,K'$ since on these charts they are spectrum morphisms. For each chart the affine closed pinching pushout node gives unique gluing into any scheme $H$. For two charts, cover their overlap by affine opens and apply this same uniqueness there; scheme-morphism gluing gives a unique global map into $H$. Hence this construction is a pushout. By uniqueness of pushouts it is canonically the specified $W$, compatibly with both maps. In particular its sheaf and its topology, not merely an abstract affine presentation, have now been established.

source.place: Tag 07RT, localization and final gluing paragraphs

proof.text: We check applicability also to $Z$. The map $U\to X$ is affine: cover $X$ by affine opens $V$ whose maps into $S$ factor through affine opens $O$ of $S$. Such a cover exists by the affine-basis node. Then $T_O$ is affine and $U_V=V\times_O T_O$ is affine by the affine-spectrum fibre-product node. The target-local criterion makes $U\to X$ affine. The map $U\to Y$ is a closed immersion by closed-immersion base change. It is a thickening: locally on affine opens of $T^+$ its ideal is generated on the pullback by images of elements of $I=\ker(A'\to A)$. The quotient-spectrum and radical nodes show $I$ consists of nilpotents because the original closed immersion is surjective on points. Every element of the extended ideal is a finite sum of multiples of such images, hence nilpotent (for nilpotence exponents $n_i$, expand power $1+\sum(n_i-1)$). The same two nodes show the pullback closed immersion is surjective on points. Thus steps 1--3 apply both to $(S,T,T^+)$ and $(X,U,Y)$, giving the specified pushouts by their universal properties.

The construction also proves open restriction. For an open $O\subseteq W$, regard it as an open in $V$ using $|V|=|W|$. Step 1 restricts to the identical sheaf formula, and steps 2--3 prove its pushout universal property. Thus $O$ is the pushout of its inverse images in $V,K',K$. For compatible maps $X\to H$, $Y\to H$, their unique extension $h$ therefore has $h^{-1}(H_0)$ as the pushout of the three indicated inverse-image schemes for every open $H_0\subseteq H$. This includes arbitrary, nonaffine opens: the proof of step 3 uses affine covers, not affineness of their intersections.

source.place: Tag 07RT, restriction of the fibre-product sheaf and local gluing construction

proof.text: Let $P_0$ be any affine open of $P$. Since $S\to P$ is a thickening by the existing pushout node, $S_0$ is affine by the affine description of a closed immersion. Then $T_0$ is affine since $T\to S$ is affine, and $T^+_0$ is affine by the affine-thickening lemma. Open restriction (step 5) says $P_0$ is their pushout. The affine closed pinching node says $\operatorname{Spec}(B\times_A A')$ is the same pushout. The unique compatible isomorphism between these pushouts is induced on rings by the canonical map $R\to B\times_A A'$, so that map is an isomorphism. The closed immersion gives $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, and its homeomorphism makes the kernel nil by the quotient-spectrum and radical nodes. This argument works for every affine $P_0$, not only the constructed chart cover.

source.place: Tag 07RT, compatible affine opens and structure-sheaf description

proof.text:
Similarly fix any affine open $Z_0\subseteq Z$ mapping into $P_0$. The thickening $X\to Z$ makes $X_0$ affine. Affineness of $U\to X$ makes $U_0$ affine, and the affine-thickening lemma makes $Y_0$ affine. Step 5 and the affine pinching node identify $E=D\times_C C'$ canonically. The original isomorphism defining $U$ restricts to these inverse images, so the affine fibre-product node identifies
$$C=D\otimes_B A=C'\otimes_{A'}A=C'/IC'.$$
For the last identification the maps are $c'\otimes\bar a'\mapsto a'c'\bmod IC'$ and $\bar c'\mapsto c'\otimes1$. Changing a lift by $i\in I$ changes the first expression by $ic'$, and the balancing relation checks both inverse equations. These are algebra identifications over the indicated bases.

source.place: Tag 07RV, affine calculation with D, C prime, and C prime modulo I C prime

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] with $N=D$, $M'=C'$ and the isomorphism of step 7. Its glued module is the underlying $R$-module of $E=D\times_C C'$. It gives bijective canonical maps $E\otimes_R B\to D$ and $E\otimes_R A'\to C'$. Each is also a unital ring map: on pure tensors its formula is $e\otimes b\mapsto p_D(e)b$, respectively $e\otimes a'\mapsto p_{C'}(e)a'$, which preserves products of pure tensors and the unit, and hence all products by distributivity. Thus they are algebra isomorphisms. The affine fibre-product node turns them into the restrictions of the two canonical scheme maps $X\to Z\times_P S$ and $Y\to Z\times_P T^+$. Affine opens of $P$ and then of their inverse images in $Z$ cover these schemes. The local inverses agree on overlaps because they invert the same canonical map. Scheme-morphism gluing gives global inverses.

source.place: Tag 07RV, final paragraph, reduction to Tag 07RU

proof.text: Finally all comparisons commute with restriction. The maps $R\to B\times_A A'$ and $E\to D\times_C C'$ send a section to its two restrictions; restricting it first gives the same pair by the sheaf restriction axioms. The tensor maps send $e\otimes b$ to $p_D(e)b$ and $e\otimes a'$ to $p_{C'}(e)a'$; every restriction is a ring map commuting with $p_D,p_{C'}$, so these formulas commute with restriction on generators and hence on every tensor. Quotient comparison sends a class of $c'$ to $c'\otimes1$, also preserved by restriction. The inverse maps commute as well by uniqueness of inverses. This proves compatibility also for smaller opens not principal in the original chart. None of the arguments required flatness, finite presentation, or a common nilpotence exponent; empty opens and zero coordinate rings are allowed.

statement_change.what: The isomorphism of the two T-fibres was not required to be over T. Without this condition there need not be an induced map Z to P: take i and a to be identities on a scheme T with a nontrivial automorphism σ, take X=Y=T with identity structural maps, and use σ as overlap identification.
